## How to review

1. Verses: do the listed ayat really contain what each claim says? Is any claim stronger than its ayat?

4. Omissions: anything the verses say that readers need and the chapter leaves out?
5. No added facts: no name, number, place, reason, emotion or sequence beyond the ayat; no implied chronology.
6. No depiction of any prophet, angel or jinn.
7. Theology and etiquette: cautious wording about prophets; no verdicts; no legal or medical ruling.

11. Titles and honorifics: bare names in the draft; honorifics added at render time.

## 1. The Companions of the Ditch  (`#the-companions-of-the-ditch`)

Cited ayat: 85:4-9

> **85:4** قُتِلَ أَصْحَٰبُ ٱلْأُخْدُودِ
>
> **85:5** ٱلنَّارِ ذَاتِ ٱلْوَقُودِ
>
> **85:6** إِذْ هُمْ عَلَيْهَا قُعُودٌ
>
> **85:7** وَهُمْ عَلَىٰ مَا يَفْعَلُونَ بِٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ شُهُودٌ
>
> **85:8** وَمَا نَقَمُوا۟ مِنْهُمْ إِلَّآ أَن يُؤْمِنُوا۟ بِٱللَّهِ ٱلْعَزِيزِ ٱلْحَمِيدِ
>
> **85:9** ٱلَّذِى لَهُۥ مُلْكُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ وَٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىْءٍ شَهِيدٌ

### Claims

**c1** (85:4): The Quran says that the Companions of the Ditch were slain, a wording that is also read as a curse on them.

**c2** (85:5): The ayat speak of the fire full of fuel.

**c3** (85:6): They were sitting by it.

**c4** (85:7): They were witnesses to what they did to the believers.

**c5** (85:8): They resented the believers only because they believed in God, the Mighty, the Praiseworthy.

**c6** (85:9): God is the One to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and God is a witness over all things.

### One-minute summary

The Quran says that the Companions of the Ditch were slain, and speaks of a fire full of fuel by which they sat [c1][c2][c3]. They resented the believers only because they believed in God, and God is a witness over all things [c5][c6].

### Complete story

The Quran says that the Companions of the Ditch were slain, a wording that is also read as a curse on them [c1]. The ayat speak of the fire full of fuel [c2]. They were sitting by it [c3]. They were witnesses to what they did to the believers [c4]. They resented the believers only because they believed in God, the Mighty, the Praiseworthy [c5]. God is the One to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and God is a witness over all things [c6].

### Deep study

- The Quran says that the Companions of the Ditch were slain, a wording that is also read as a curse on them (85:4) [c1].
- The ayat speak of the fire full of fuel (85:5) [c2].
- They were sitting by it (85:6) [c3].
- They were witnesses to what they did to the believers (85:7) [c4].
- They resented the believers only because they believed in God, the Mighty, the Praiseworthy (85:8) [c5].
- God is the One to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and God is a witness over all things (85:9) [c6].

### Kids mode

The Quran tells of people who sat by a fire and watched what was done to the believers [c2][c3][c4]. They were angry with the believers only because the believers believed in God [c5].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): The passage names the believers' belief in God as the only thing the others resented, and ends by saying that God is a witness over all things [c5][c6]. One reading is that the ayat console those who are wronged for their belief [c5][c6].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: who the Companions of the Ditch were, where or when they lived, who the believers were, or how many; the Quran does not say.
- Not established: the ayat do not state that the believers were thrown into the fire; they speak of the fire and of what the Companions did to the believers.
- Not established: whether the ditch of the title and the fire are one thing; the ayat name the ditch only in 85:4.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the king, the place and the persons of the accounts later tradition tells about the Companions of the Ditch; none is used here.
